about.title: Martinez Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall at a Martinez grocery store, an office along Alhambra Avenue, or an apartment complex near downtown can leave you with more than bruises — it can mean missed work and mounting medical bills. Martinez sees a steady flow of injury collisions each year, and falls on unsafe property follow a similar pattern: they're often preventable, and often disputed by the property owner's insurer. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard before you got hurt. That's why what happens in the first days after a fall matters so much — photos of the spill, torn carpet, or broken step, plus any surveillance footage, can shape the entire claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options under Contra Costa County premises rules.

whyChoose.title: Why Martinez Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify what evidence supports that before it disappears.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many stores and businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks, so an early request to preserve it can be critical to a Martinez claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the fall — your share of fault simply adjusts the outcome, it doesn't erase your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Martinez?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned — say, a walkway maintained by the City of Martinez or Contra Costa County — that window can shrink dramatically, sometimes to just six months for a claim notice. It's worth having someone check ownership early.

items.question: What if I partly caused my own fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you were distracted or not watching your step. Your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't automatically barred. An attorney can help sort out how much responsibility, if any, actually falls on you versus the property owner.

items.question: Does LawProactive represent me directly?
items.answer: No — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We simply match you with an independent attorney in Contra Costa County who can review your fall and explain what documentation, like photos or surveillance requests, might strengthen your position.
